knownGaps.observation: Map.fold inserts dict2 into dict1, so second dictionary wins. Required expectation remains first dictionary wins.
Inline arithmetic uses default unchecked operators/pown, not the admitted checked Int32 boundary. No runtime conformance is claimed here.
Existing divide returns decimal and throws on zero. Canonical Decimal.div returns Maybe<Decimal>, Nothing for zero.
ToString() uses current culture and retains authored scale. Canonical text is invariant positional, with trailing fractional zeros removed.

outsideInitialInventory: Trigonometry, dates/times, Int fixed-width conversions beyond Int32, decimal parsing/conversion/rounding, and collection operations not enumerated here need a reviewed contract extension; unknown operations fail validation.

discrepancies.decision: Python/Elm integerDivide(7,0) yields 0; MoonBit exact-integer extension raises DivisionByZero. dotnet-sdk-v1 explicitly adopts the latter as an extension, not Elm parity. Int32 checked overflow is also a .NET restriction.

Python compares code points; Elm compares UTF-16 units. dotnet-sdk-v1 selects Elm's ordinal UTF-16 order. Supplemental strings remain admitted; supplementary Char is an explicit representation exclusion.

Python abs delegates to builtins.abs and returns +0 for -0. MoonBit abs_float tests value < 0.0, so its else branch preserves -0. dotnet-sdk-v1 selects Python/IEEE absolute value +0 and retains the signed-zero case as required.

Python uses 50-digit half-up context, MoonBit classic decimal truncates at exponent -32 and checked API is separate. Admit exact Decimal96 results only. Preserve outside-domain reference observations in excluded cases; never round them to .NET output.
Morphir Result<error,value>; F# and Gleam host Result<value,error> reverse generic parameter meanings. Adapters must map payloads, not generic positions.
